title: Healthy Thanksgiving Recipes That’ll Make You Feel Great
summary: Olive oil mashed potatoes, baked apples and more lighter and brighter dishes for a balanced and vibrant feast.

Advertisement


By Samantha Cassetty


Samantha Cassetty is a registered dietitian nutritionist.


Published Nov. 13, 2025


Updated Oct. 2, 2026


[Thanksgiving](https://cooking.nytimes.com/thanksgiving) comes only once a year. So even if you typically aim to eat a well-balanced diet, helping yourself to a scoop of buttery[mashed potato casserole](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1013923-mashed-potato-casserole?art=100000010508972) or a generous slice of[apple crumb pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026155-dutch-apple-pie?art=100000010508972) on the year’s biggest food holiday isn’t only OK, it’s an important part of the celebration. Holiday foods often carry with them family traditions and memories, and enjoying them is one way we honor those connections. (Remember: What you eat most of the time matters far more than what you eat in a single day.)


Healthy means different things to different people. But, according to the[Dietary Guidelines for Americans](https://www.dietaryguidelines.gov/) (updated by the Health and Human Services Department and the Agriculture Department every five years), the[American Heart Association](https://www.heart.org/en/healthy-living/healthy-eating/eat-smart/nutrition-basics/your-guide-to-healthy-eating-habits-that-stick) , and the[American Diabetes Association](https://diabetes.org/food-nutrition/eating-healthy) , it’s pretty straightforward.


All three groups recommend filling your plate with plenty of fruits and vegetables, cooking with heart-healthy fats like extra-virgin olive oil and avocado oil, and including beans, nuts, seeds and whole grains whenever possible. They also recommend being mindful of added sugars, processed meats, and[ultraprocessed foods](https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/06/well/eat/ultraprocessed-foods-harmful-health.html) , which is where much of our dietary sodium hides. Finally, you should keep an eye on butter and sugar intake, but unless you have a medical condition that requires it, most people don’t need to eliminate them completely.


If you want to take your table in a healthier direction, keep it simple. Many Thanksgiving staples, like[turkey](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015474-simple-roast-turkey?art=100000010508972) ,[roasted brussels sprouts](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1890-roasted-brussels-sprouts-with-garlic?art=100000010508972) and[sautéed green beans,](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1025432-sauteed-green-beans?art=100000010508972) are naturally wholesome as they are. But heavier dishes, like[sweet potato casserole](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1021635-sweet-potato-casserole?art=100000010508972) or[apple pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/12320-apple-pie?art=100000010508972) , can be swapped for[roasted sweet potatoes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024418-roasted-sweet-potatoes?art=100000010508972) or an[apple crisp](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022569-apple-crisp?art=100000010508972) . (Or not, and you just get back to balanced eating the next day.) However you approach it, these 30 recipes can help you build a healthier and more colorful meal, which is no less fun or delicious.


## 1.[Orange Ginger Brussels Sprouts](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1025744-orange-ginger-brussels-sprouts?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Ghazalle Badiozamani for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Barrett Washburne.


Ali Slagle’s five-star roasted brussels sprouts add a bit of bright color and flavor to your spread. The citrusy dressing is a welcome contrast to richer Thanksgiving dishes, and the dish tastes as good at room temperature as it does hot, which gives you a little flexibility with timing.


Recipe: **[Orange Ginger Brussels Sprouts](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1025744-orange-ginger-brussels-sprouts?art=100000010508972)**


Advertisement


## 2.[Ginger-Scallion Broccoli Salad](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/776098177-ginger-scallion-broccoli-salad?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Christopher Testani for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


In Kay Chun’s 20-minute salad, the lively dressing — a mix of extra virgin olive oil, ginger, lemon juice and miso — is what earns it a spot at your holiday meal. The broccoli cooks on the stove top, which frees up the oven for everything else. Try tossing in white beans or edamame if you need a more substantial option for vegan and vegetarian eaters.


Recipe: **[Ginger-Scallion Broccoli Salad](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/776098177-ginger-scallion-broccoli-salad?art=100000010508972)**


## 3.[Roast Squash With Crispy Chickpeas and Feta](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1027410-roast-squash-with-crispy-chickpeas-and-feta?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Ryan Liebe for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Barrett Washburne. Prop Stylist: Megan Hedgpeth.


Dan Pelosi’s three-squash platter looks like a centerpiece, and with chickpeas in the mix, it’s hearty enough to serve as a vegetarian main. Every bite brings a happy mix of smoky, spicy, sweet and briny flavors.


Recipe: **[Roast Squash With Crispy Chickpeas and Feta](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1027410-roast-squash-with-crispy-chickpeas-and-feta?art=100000010508972)**


## 4.[Roasted Cauliflower Gratin With Tomatoes and Goat Cheese](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015968-roasted-cauliflower-gratin-with-tomatoes-and-goat-cheese?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Armando Rafael for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Monica Pierini.


Put a veggie-packed spin on the usual potato gratin with Martha Rose Shulman’s roasted cauliflower version. Warmly spiced tomato sauce and tangy goat cheese give it plenty of zing. You can make this a couple of days in advance, so it’s an easy dish to work into your Thanksgiving prep.


Recipe: **[Roasted Cauliflower Gratin With Tomatoes and Goat Cheese](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015968-roasted-cauliflower-gratin-with-tomatoes-and-goat-cheese?art=100000010508972)**


Advertisement


## 5.[Cacio e Pepe Green Beans](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/762811983-cacio-e-pepe-green-beans?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Rachel Vanni for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


Sheela Prakash’s version of the holiday favorite has a subtle Italian twist, inspired by[cacio e pepe](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1017304-cacio-e-pepe?art=100000010508972) . The beans are glossy with black pepper-infused olive oil and a generous sprinkle of Pecorino Romano. It’s an easy, one-pan side that still feels special.


Recipe: **[Cacio e Pepe Green Beans](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/762811983-cacio-e-pepe-green-beans?art=100000010508972)**


## 6.[Roasted Butternut Squash Salad With Spicy Scallion Dressing](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/761873488-roasted-butternut-squash-salad-with-spicy-scallion-dressing?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Rachel Vanni for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Monica Pierini.


Herbs and spices complement the natural sweetness of butternut squash and orange in Ashley Lonsdale’s salad. Balance out your Thanksgiving Day workload by making this ahead; it tastes even better as it sits.


Recipe: **[Roasted Butternut Squash Salad With Spicy Green Sauce](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/761873488-roasted-butternut-squash-salad-with-spicy-scallion-dressing?art=100000010508972)**


## 7.[Simple Roast Turkey](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015474-simple-roast-turkey?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


This turkey from Melissa Clark has earned its spot at the center of countless holiday meals, and for good reason. With more than 5,000 five-star reviews, readers called it “moist” and “picture-perfect.” Make this, and you’ll see why this bird has become a holiday legend.


Recipe: **[Simple Roast Turkey](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015474-simple-roast-turkey?art=100000010508972)**


Advertisement


## 8.[Roasted Lemon Caper Brussels Sprouts](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/762981880-roasted-lemon-caper-brussels-sprouts?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Christopher Testani for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


These brussels sprouts shine thanks to Sheela Prakash’s briny dressing of lemon, Dijon and capers. The dish is simple enough for a regular weeknight, but special enough to share space with your other sides.


Recipe: **[Roasted Lemon Caper Brussels Sprouts](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/762981880-roasted-lemon-caper-brussels-sprouts?art=100000010508972)**


## 9.[Olive Oil Mashed Potatoes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015335-olive-oil-mashed-potatoes?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Christopher Testani for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Rebecca Jurkevich.


Made with extra-virgin olive oil instead of butter, David Tanis’s mashed potatoes are smooth, garlicky and full of flavor — not to mention vegan and easy to make.


Recipe: **[Olive Oil Mashed Potatoes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015335-olive-oil-mashed-potatoes?art=100000010508972)**


## 10. K[ale Salad With Pickled Raisin Vinaigrette](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/762981191-kale-salad-with-pickled-raisin-vinaigrette?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Rachel Vanni for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Monica Pierini.


Sheela Prakash’s kale salad will win over guests with its pickled raisin and honey vinaigrette, which sets it apart from more traditional versions. As a bonus, everything can be prepped in advance.


Recipe: **[Kale Salad With Pickled Raisin Vinaigrette](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/762981191-kale-salad-with-pickled-raisin-vinaigrette?art=100000010508972)**


Advertisement


## 11.[Wild Rice Dressing With Mushrooms and Chile Crisp](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1021586-wild-rice-dressing-with-mushrooms-and-chile-crisp?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


NIk Sharma for The New York Times (Photography and Styling)


Shake up the menu with Nik Sharma’s modern take on wild rice dressing. It combines earthy mushrooms, sweet dried cranberries and chewy rice, but the chile crisp is the cherry on top: a crunchy, spicy finish that ties it all together.


Recipe: **[Wild Rice Dressing With Mushrooms and Chile Crisp](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1021586-wild-rice-dressing-with-mushrooms-and-chile-crisp?art=100000010508972)**


## 12.[French Lentil Salad](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026766-french-lentil-salad?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Linda Xiao for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Maggie Ruggiero. Prop Stylist: Sophia Eleni Pappas.


“This was outstanding!” wrote one reader about Lisa Donovan’s hearty French lentil salad. Made with thyme, rosemary, parsley, tarragon and dill, it’s an herby, flavorful vegetarian side or main. To make it vegan, swap the honey for maple syrup.


Recipe: **[French Lentil Salad](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026766-french-lentil-salad?art=100000010508972)**


## 13.[Brussels Sprout Salad With Pomegranate and Pistachios](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026017-brussels-sprout-salad-with-pomegranate-and-pistachios?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


This salad from Sheela Prakash sparkles with jewel-toned pistachios and pomegranate seeds. The bulgur — a nod to tabbouleh — gives this vibrant dish enough heft to double as a vegetarian main. The final result: “Outstanding!”


Recipe: **[Brussels Sprout Salad With Pomegranate and Pistachios](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026017-brussels-sprout-salad-with-pomegranate-and-pistachios?art=100000010508972)**


Advertisement


## 14.[Whole Roasted Cauliflower With Almond-Herb Sauce](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1017902-whole-roasted-cauliflower-with-almond-herb-sauce?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


John Kernick for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


This whole roasted cauliflower is a stunning vegetarian side or main. The mix of almonds, garlic and herbs gives it a rich flavor that’s balanced by the tanginess of vinegar. Any variety of cauliflower works, but a colorful one adds extra flair to your holiday table.


Recipe: **[Whole Roasted Cauliflower With Almond-Herb Sauce](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1017902-whole-roasted-cauliflower-with-almond-herb-sauce?art=100000010508972)**


## 15.[Ina Garten’s Perfect Roast Chicken](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026751-ina-gartens-perfect-roast-chicken?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Rebecca Jurkevich.


“This recipe lives up to its name,” says one reader of Ina Garten’s much-loved roast chicken. Stuffed with lemon, garlic and thyme, then brushed with butter, this roast chicken is a lower-fuss alternative for smaller gatherings.


Recipe: **[Ina Garten’s Perfect Roast Chicken](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026751-ina-gartens-perfect-roast-chicken?art=100000010508972)**


## 16.[Cranberry-Orange Relish](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1012886-cranberry-orange-relish?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Linda Xiao for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Monica Pierini.


Martha Rose Shulman’s cranberry-orange relish is a citrusy alternative to traditional cranberry sauce. Fresh orange and honey balance the tart cranberries, and pecans add subtle crunch. Make extra to enjoy on leftover turkey sandwiches or to add to yogurt for breakfast.


Recipe: **[Cranberry-Orange Relish](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1012886-cranberry-orange-relish?art=100000010508972)**


Advertisement


## 17.[Buttermilk-Brined Turkey Breast](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1021522-buttermilk-brined-turkey-breast?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Romulo Yanes for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Vivian Lui.


Samin Nosrat’s turkey breast is a fantastic centerpiece for a smaller Thanksgiving. The tangy, salted buttermilk works its magic overnight (or longer, if you plan ahead), yielding juicy meat and a beautifully burnished skin. Once marinated, it roasts to perfection in under an hour — a foolproof showstopper.


Recipe: **[Buttermilk-Brined Turkey Breast](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1021522-buttermilk-brined-turkey-breast?art=100000010508972)**


## 18.[Caramelized Shallot Gravy](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026173-caramelized-shallot-gravy?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Armando Rafael for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Samantha Seneviratne.


This vegan gravy from Carolina Gelen is rich and versatile: Serve it over turkey or any holiday side, such as mashed potatoes or stuffing. Tip: Use a lower-sodium soy sauce to decrease the salt content by almost 40-percent without sacrificing flavor.


Recipe: **[Caramelized Shallot Gravy](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026173-caramelized-shallot-gravy?art=100000010508972)**


## 19.[Roasted Sweet Potatoes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024418-roasted-sweet-potatoes?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Christopher Testani for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


Lidey Heuck’s roasted sweet potatoes emerge from the oven tender with crisp, caramelized edges. “It’s so easy,” one reader said, “it shouldn’t be legal to make for Thanksgiving.” Others suggest dressing it up with smoked paprika, gochujang and soy sauce, or a touch of maple syrup for sweetness.


Recipe: **[Roasted Sweet Potatoes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024418-roasted-sweet-potatoes?art=100000010508972)**


Advertisement


## 20.[Baked Apples](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020471-baked-apples?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Christopher Testani for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Yossy Arefi.


Baked apples check a lot of boxes for holiday entertaining: They’re simple, gluten-free and can be made dairy-free or vegan to suit your guests. Dorie Greenspan fills hers with dried apple rings and candied ginger, but you can use another dried fruit, such as raisins or cherries. A dollop of whipped cream or ice cream is optional, but nice.


Recipe: **[Baked Apples](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020471-baked-apples?art=100000010508972)**


## 21.[Vegan Pumpkin Cheesecake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015404-vegan-pumpkin-cheesecake?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Linda Xiao for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Barrett Washburne.


If you’re on the hunt for a five-star vegan dessert, look no further than this cheesecake from Isa Chandra Moskowitz. One reader describes it as “silky, fresh and absolutely delightful.” Instead of cream cheese, soaked cashews are blended with the banana, silken tofu, pumpkin purée and pumpkin pie spices.


Recipe: **[Vegan Pumpkin Cheesecake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015404-vegan-pumpkin-cheesecake?art=100000010508972)**


## 22.[Roasted Potatoes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024348-roasted-potatoes?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Christopher Testani for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


For the best roasted potatoes you’ll ever make, try Lidey Heuck’s recipe. You can dress it up with herbs or spices, or keep it simple with olive oil and salt. Either way, it’s the kind of side that belongs on every table — on Thanksgiving and throughout the year.


Recipe: **[Roasted Potatoes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024348-roasted-potatoes?art=100000010508972)**


Advertisement


## 23.[Spicy Peanut and Pumpkin Soup](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1019759-spicy-peanut-and-pumpkin-soup?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Linda Xiao for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Monica Pierini.


Yewande Komolafe’s spicy pumpkin soup, which draws from Nigerian cuisine, is beautiful on the table. The blend of pumpkin, coconut milk and peanut butter gives the soup a creamy depth, while the ginger, garlic and chile add gentle heat that one reader described as “absolutely delicious!”


Recipe: **[Spicy Peanut and Pumpkin Soup](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1019759-spicy-peanut-and-pumpkin-soup?art=100000010508972)**


## 24.[Gregory Gourdet’s Carrot Salad With Oranges and Cashews](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026354-gregory-gourdets-carrot-salad-with-oranges-and-cashews?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


“Gregory, you genius!” one reader wrote about this dish’s flavors. With chiles, lime and cashews, it’s spicy, crunchy and ready to disappear fast at any gathering. Case in point: “Everyone raved about it, there was not a single spoonful leftover.”


Recipe: **[Gregory Gourdet’s Carrot Salad With Oranges and Cashews](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026354-gregory-gourdets-carrot-salad-with-oranges-and-cashews?art=100000010508972)**


## 25.[Caramel Pears With Rosemary, Honey and Walnuts](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020501-caramel-pears-with-rosemary-honey-and-walnuts?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Andrew Scrivani for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Devon Knight


David Tanis’s caramel pears, described by one reader as “lovely and simple with a scoop of vanilla ice cream,” is quite the dessert. Baked with star anise, cinnamon and honey, the pears are cooked until soft for a rustic, elegant finale.


Recipe: **[Caramel Pears With Rosemary, Honey and Walnuts](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020501-caramel-pears-with-rosemary-honey-and-walnuts?art=100000010508972)**


Advertisement


## 26.[Broccoli With Sizzled Nuts and Dates](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024947-broccoli-with-sizzled-nuts-and-dates?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Cyd Raftus McDowell.


“My broccoli-hating husband absolutely devoured this,” wrote one reader about Sohla El-Waylly’s sweet-and-savory side. Dates and mixed nuts give humble broccoli a Thanksgiving-worthy upgrade that just might convert any skeptics at the table.


Recipe: **[Broccoli With Sizzled Nuts and Dates](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024947-broccoli-with-sizzled-nuts-and-dates?art=100000010508972)**


## 27.[Turnip Greens](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1025266-turnip-greens?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


Vallery Lomas skips the usual smoked meats in favor of smoked paprika in this healthier spin on the Southern classic. If you’re watching your salt intake, swap in low-sodium stock. The greens will still soak up plenty of flavor.


Recipe: **[Turnip Greens](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1025266-turnip-greens?art=100000010508972)**


## 28.[Squash and Spinach Salad With Sesame Vinaigrette](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1023809-squash-and-spinach-salad-with-sesame-vinaigrette?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Joel Goldberg for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Barrett Washburne.


Kay Chun’s roasted squash salad is sweet, nutty and full of color. A triple-sesame vinaigrette ties it all together, prompting one reader to call it “splendid.” It’s great as a Thanksgiving side or a plant-based main. If you’d like to make it even more filling, add rinsed and drained canned beans.


Recipe: **[Squash and Spinach Salad With Sesame Vinaigrette](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1023809-squash-and-spinach-salad-with-sesame-vinaigrette?art=100000010508972)**


Advertisement


## 29.[Vegan Poblano Macaroni and Cheese](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022739-vegan-poblano-macaroni-and-cheese?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Bryan Gardner for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Barrett Washburne. Prop Stylist: Paige Hicks.


If you’re looking for a dairy-free, vegan main or side, give Jocelyn Ramirez’s mac and cheese a try. Cashews and potatoes are blended together to create a silky sauce. Carrots lend color, and nutritional yeast delivers that cheesy flavor. You can even make it gluten free by using a gluten-free pasta of your choice.


Recipe: **[Vegan Poblano Macaroni and Cheese](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022739-vegan-poblano-macaroni-and-cheese?art=100000010508972)**


## 30.[Apple Crisp](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022569-apple-crisp?art=100000010508972)


Credit...


Johnny Miller for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews. Prop Stylist: Christina Lane.


Consider swapping a traditional double-crusted apple pie for Genevieve Ko’s crisp with a golden, nutty topping that readers call “the best part.” It’s just sweet enough, and it’s easy to make gluten-free.


Recipe: **[Apple Crisp](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022569-apple-crisp?art=100000010508972)**
